name: bash
summary: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)
description: Run a shell command in the session's working directory and wait for it to finish. The command has no terminal and its standard input is empty, so a program that waits for input fails or hangs until the timeout. Standard output and standard error come back together, followed by the exit code when it is not zero. Only the first {shell_output_chars} characters of output are returned. A command that runs past its timeout ({shell_timeout_ms} ms unless the call sets one, at most {shell_max_timeout_ms} ms) is stopped with its process group. Commands run without an operating system sandbox.
guidance: Use bash for file operations like ls, rg, find.
Commands in bash get no terminal and no input. Use the non-interactive form of a command (such as -y, --no-edit, --no-pager, or a message given with -m), and never start an editor, a pager or a REPL.

timeout.description: Timeout in milliseconds, more than 0 and at most {shell_max_timeout_ms}. Omit for {shell_timeout_ms}.

description.description: A few plain words saying what the command does. The user sees this.
